newsitem.title: GERMANY: CalPERS CEO says still unhappy with ADM.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS CEO says still unhappy with ADM.

text.p: The head of California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said on Tuesday he was still unhappy with Archer Daniels Midland Co, despite the settlement of two lawsuits which had been dogging it.
"We are still not happy, the suit notwithstanding," said Jim Burton, chief executive of the largest U.S. pension fund CalPERS, which owns 3.5 million ADM shares.
Burton, who is in Europe to promote investment in California, said he was scheduled to meet with the troubled agribusiness company on October 7, ahead of its annual meeting on October 17.

On Friday ADM settled a lawsuit alleging price fixing in the lysine, citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup market for $65 million, although it did not admit to any wrongdoing. The lawsuits came after a federal investigation.

In the wake of the probe CalPERS and another pension fund, the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund, proposed a change in the company's by-laws requesting that the ADM board be composed of a majority of independent directors, to be voted on by shareholders.

"We intend to pursue our shareholder resolution vigorously," said Burton. "We are unhappy with the make-up of the board. We are don't believe that they are following the intents of their own governance committee."
Earlier on Monday CalPERS issued a statement from its California headquarters saying the ADM board "fails to meet even a watered-down version of independence."
